framework_rationale: The board must approve or amend a specific budget request; Situation-Complication-Resolution puts the diagnosis (a retention problem) before testing the CRO plan and proposing the alternative, so the problem comes before the solution

candidates.text: Growth slowed because we lost customers, not deals: higher churn explains 80.4% of the €5.6M fall in net new ARR, concentrated in first-year customers after the onboarding cut. Fund retention first (restore onboarding, €0.8M) with a gated first wave of 10 AEs, for €2.0M a year instead of €3.6M, rather than 30 AEs whose 2026 yield is at most an estimated €4.5M, not the €9M promised.
Approve the CRO plan but phase it: hire 30 AEs over 2026 and add a pricing response to the new competitor.
The slowdown is a retention problem; freeze growth investment until churn is back to 2024 levels.

governing_thought: Growth slowed because we lost customers, not deals: higher churn explains 80.4% of the €5.6M fall in net new ARR, concentrated in first-year customers after the onboarding cut. Fund retention first (restore onboarding, €0.8M) with a gated first wave of 10 AEs, for €2.0M a year instead of €3.6M, rather than 30 AEs whose 2026 yield is at most an estimated €4.5M, not the €9M promised.

key_line.message: Growth slowed because churn more than doubled to €7.8M and explains 80.4% of the €5.6M fall in net new ARR; the sales engine kept growing pipeline 18.0% at a stable win rate
The leak sits in the first year: new customers churned 26% versus 12% in 2024 after onboarding was cut to save €0.8M, costing €2.5M of ARR
The 30-AE plan does not hold: with a 9-month ramp it yields at most €4.5M in 2026, not €9M, for €3.6M a year, and pours new customers into the leak
A retention-first plan for €2.0M a year identifies up to €5.3M of the €5.6M needed, with AE wave 2 gated on retention

target.statement: Restore net new ARR to its 2024 level (€10.4M), i.e. recover the €5.6M lost in 2025 (inferred target; no 2026 target in the sources)

levers.statement: Restore the onboarding team to its pre-cut size and bring first-year churn back to the 2024 rate of 12%
levers.validate: Time to first value back to 21 days and 90-day churn of the Q1-Q2 2026 cohort, reviewed at the June 2026 board

levers.statement: Recover expansion ARR to the 2024 level through customer-success led adoption of customers who never fully implemented
levers.validate: Root cause of the expansion decline (H6 unresolved): expansion pipeline from implemented accounts by end Q2 2026

levers.statement: Hire a first wave of 10 AEs in Q1 2026
levers.validate: Ramp curve of the 2025 AE hires (A001) before offer letters; month-6 productivity of wave 1

gap.how_closed: Not closed with evidence in 2026: candidates are reducing the 9% churn of mature customers and AE wave 2, released only if gate G1 is met; we state the gap rather than overclaim, and all three levers are upper bounds

current_plan.statement: CRO proposal: hire 30 account executives in Q1 2026 for €3.6M a year, promised to add €9M of new ARR in 2026

cost_if_kept.statement: at least €4.5M of the promised €9M new ARR would not materialise in 2026, while the €2.5M first-year churn leak stays open

options.statement: Keep the CRO plan: 30 AEs in Q1 2026 (at most €4.5M new ARR in 2026, churn untouched)
Retention first: restore onboarding (€0.8M) plus a first wave of 10 AEs (€1.2M), AE wave 2 gated
Restore onboarding only, no new AEs in 2026

asks.statement: Reject the 30-AE hiring plan as proposed (€3.6M a year, €9M of 2026 new ARR not achievable)
Approve €0.8M a year to restore the onboarding team to its pre-cut size from Q1 2026
Approve a first wave of 10 AEs (€1.2M a year) in Q1 2026
Reallocate the remaining €1.6M of the requested budget to a reserve released for AE wave 2 only when gate G1 is met

gates.criterion: Median time to first value at or below 21 days and annualised first-year churn of the 2026 cohort at or below 12%, and wave-1 AEs on the ramp assumed in A001
Expansion pipeline from implemented accounts on track for the 2024 expansion level

kpis.name: Net new ARR (ARR bridge: new, expansion, churn)
New ARR per AE versus ramp curve
